statements.text: A client recently had that kind of reaction to some new ads from us.
statements.source: before_publishing: do not imply the ads were poor
statements.why: Follows a list of flaws in ads (generic headline, off tone, photo), so it implies the client's ads were poor, which is kept out.

statements.text: They weren't sure they loved them, and they hadn't finished their review.
statements.why: Matches the client's tentative reaction and unfinished review.

statements.text: I welcomed specific edits and made it clear that not using those ads was a fine answer too.
statements.why: Whitney welcomed edits and said not using the ads was fine.

statements.text: Our effort on a draft doesn't turn your approval into an obligation.
statements.why: States the approved central point and adds no event.

statements.text: That holds whether we're managing your campaigns or guiding you while you handle your own.
statements.source: before_publishing: belief-level wording confirmed for management and guided support
statements.why: Belief-level wording about both ways of working, confirmed by the team.

statements.text: We'd sent new ads for review.
statements.source: We'd sent new ads for review.
statements.why: Stated in the supported claims.

statements.text: Our team had made the proposed creative for a client's Meta campaigns.
statements.why: The team made the creative, and the call names the Meta ad side.

statements.text: We sent it over and checked in on our call to hear what they thought.
statements.why: Whitney asked on the call whether they had looked at the ads.

statements.text: "I don't think that I love them."
statements.why: Exact words of the client, placed in the moment they were said.

statements.text: They also said they hadn't finished reviewing them yet.
statements.why: Client said not yet to finalize anything.

statements.text: So this was a starting point, not a final answer.
statements.why: The reaction was tentative, not a completed rejection.

statements.text: She invited specific edits.
statements.why: Whitney invited specific tweaks or edits.

statements.text: She also said that if they'd rather not use those ads, that was fine, with no hard feelings either way.
statements.why: Matches Whitney's no-hard-feelings statement.

statements.text: Whether we manage your ads for you, or we launch your campaigns, then guide you while you run them, the same honesty applies.
statements.why: Standard close naming both ways of working, matching approved descriptors, with no program, price or link.

statements.text: Not long ago, our team sent a client new Meta ads to review.
statements.source: We'd sent new ads for review.
statements.why: Matches the real event and its timing.

statements.text: On our call, they said they weren't sure they loved them and hadn't finished looking yet.
statements.why: Matches the client's words on the call.

statements.text: I told them specific edits were welcome, and that leaving those ads unused was an option too, with no hard feelings.
statements.why: Matches Whitney's response.

statements.text: When a client recently told me they weren't sure they loved some new ads we'd sent, and that they hadn't finished reviewing them, I said two things.
statements.why: Matches the scene.

statements.text: Send any specific edits you'd like. And if you'd rather not use those ads, that's fine too.
statements.why: Faithful paraphrase of what Whitney said.

statements.text: When you hire a team to run your ads, part of what you're hiring us for is making the creative and sending it over for review.
statements.why: Whitney describes presenting new creatives for approval as part of the service.

statements.text: This came up with a client recently. They weren't sure they loved a few new ads we'd sent, and they hadn't finished reviewing them.
statements.why: Matches the scene.

statements.text: I told them edits were welcome, and if they'd rather not use them, that's completely fine. No hard feelings.
statements.why: Matches Whitney's words.

statements.text: On a recent call, a client hadn't finished reviewing some new ads from us, and their first reaction was that they didn't think they loved them.
statements.why: Matches the client's reaction.

statements.text: I told them specific edits were welcome, and that leaving those ads unused was a perfectly good answer too.
statements.why: Matches Whitney's response.

statements.text: We believe the work behind a draft is something we bring to the partnership, never a debt you settle with a yes.
statements.why: States the approved stance and adds no event.

statements.text: Our client wasn't sure they loved the new ads we'd made.
statements.why: Matches the client's tentative reaction.

statements.text: Whitney offered edits, or the option to not use them at all.
statements.why: Matches what Whitney offered.

statements.text: Making the ads didn't make approval something we were owed.
statements.why: Matches the central point.
